Eating less isn't always the answer. For years, we've been told that if we want to lose weight, we need to eat less. So we skip meals, cut portions, avoid carbs and try to get by on as little food as possible. But here's where that approach can backfire, especially in midlife. When you're constantly trying to eat less, you're often missing out on the very things that make fat loss easier to manage. Protein to help keep you full and maintain muscle. Fibre to support digestion, gut health and keep hunger in check. Food volume, so you can eat satisfying meals without consuming excessive calories. And when you're hungry all the time, it's much harder to stick to your calorie goals. You end up snacking, picking at food or overeating later in the day. The answer isn't to keep cutting calories. It's to make the calories you're eating work harder for you. Build your meals around protein, add plenty of fibre-rich foods and fill your plate with foods that give you more volume for fewer calories. You still need a calorie deficit to lose fat, but you don't need to spend your days feeling hungry and deprived. Eating smarter, not just eating less, can make all the difference. Here's how I'm approaching my 30-day fat loss phase 👇🏽. I'm not demonizing food. Halloween candy isn't bad. It's food. And no food needs to be completely off-limits for me to make progress. I'm prioritizing protein and balanced meals. Getting enough protein, carbs, fats, and fibre keeps me satisfied and makes it easier to manage my hunger throughout the day. I'm staying in a small calorie deficit, not starving myself. Fat loss comes down to consistently consuming fewer calories than I burn. I don't need to drastically slash my calories to make that happen. I'm allowing myself flexibility. Some days I might have 3 pieces of candy. Some days I might not want any. Both decisions are fine. I'm focusing on consistency, not perfection. I don't need to hit all my macros perfectly everyday to get results. If my carbs are a bit higher one day but I'm within my calorie range it's all good.  And here's something I wish more women understood. When you spend weeks or months telling yourself you can't have certain foods, eventually the restriction catches up with you. You end up overeating those foods, feeling guilty, and convincing yourself that you're the problem. That cycle isn't a lack of willpower. It's often the result of a plan that leaves no room for flexibility. You can lose fat AND enjoy your favourite foods in the process. Because the goal isn't just to lose weight. It's to build the habits that allow you to easily keep it off. #fitover40 #fatlosstips #weightloss #weightlossjourney  #fatlosscoach

My women over 40, losing weight is different from losing weight in your 20s and 30s. Your body is changing, so your strategy must change too! Here are three things that can help: 1️⃣ Start walking. It’s a low-impact exercise that’s gentle on your joints and supports your overall health without placing excessive stress on your body. 2️⃣ Lift weights. Strength training helps preserve and build the muscle mass we naturally begin losing as we age. 3️⃣ Prioritize protein. Protein supports muscle growth, recovery, and fullness—making it an essential part of your journey. Don’t just focus on losing pounds—focus on becoming stronger and healthier!
